core_obligations: Finiteness of pi: when f is locally of finite presentation, Z' -> S is locally of finite presentation as a composite, Y' -> S is locally of finite presentation as a composite of a smooth and an etale morphism, so pi : Z' -> Y' is locally of finite presentation and, being finite and hence separated and quasi-compact, is of finite presentation (proof lines 625-633).

First chain (1), (2), (3): introduce statement (4) that g^*F is of finite presentation near x', show (1) implies (4) by pullback, get (4) implies (1) by descent along the open etale covering U' -> g(U'), and then use descent along the finite morphism with the single-point fibre to obtain (4) iff (2) iff (3) (proof lines 636-654).

Second chain (a), (b), (c): examine the ring maps O_{X,x} -> O_{X',x'} -> O_{Z',z'} and O_{Y',y'} <- O_{Z',z'}; the first is faithfully flat so finite presentation of F_x is equivalent to that of g^*F_{x'}, the second is surjective and finitely presented so that is equivalent to finite presentation of G_{z'}, and the third is finite and of finite presentation with a single point in the fibre so that is equivalent to finite presentation of pi_*G_{y'} (proof lines 657-684).
proof_roadmap: Show pi is of finite presentation by composing the local finite presentation of Z' -> S and Y' -> S with finiteness of pi (proof lines 625-633).

For the neighbourhood statement, insert the auxiliary condition (4) on g^*F; pullback gives (1) => (4), descent along the etale covering g : U' -> g(U') gives (4) => (1), and descent along pi with its single-point fibre gives the remaining equivalences (proof lines 636-654).

For the local-ring statement, walk along the chain of ring maps: faithful flatness of O_{X,x} -> O_{X',x'}, surjectivity and finite presentation of O_{X',x'} -> O_{Z',z'}, and finiteness plus finite presentation of O_{Z',z'} over O_{Y',y'}, applying the finite-extension criterion each time (proof lines 657-684).
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares finite presentation of F in a neighbourhood of x with finite presentation of G near z' and of pi_*G near y', and then repeats the comparison on the local rings at those three points (statement lines 601-621). The proof first has to establish that pi itself is of finite presentation, which uses that Z' -> S and Y' -> S are locally of finite presentation and that a finite morphism which is locally of finite presentation is of finite presentation (proof lines 625-633). The two chains then run through different mechanisms: the neighbourhood chain needs an auxiliary condition on the pullback g^*F plus descent along the open etale covering and along the finite morphism with a single point in its fibre, while the local-ring chain needs the faithfully flat, then surjective finite, then finite presentation structure of the three local ring maps (proof lines 636-684). The organisation is what is non-formal here, since each individual implication is a citation, so the claim is H2.
